entries.title: Ezekiel 25:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Aha - When thou shouldest have pitied, thou didst proudly insult over my people.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The men of the east - The Arabians, associates of Nebuchadnezzar, who recompensed their service, with giving them this country when it was conquered, as it was five years after the desolation of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rabbah - The royal city, called since Philadelphia from the king of Egypt who built it. The Ammonites - The land they dwelt in.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Know - Thus God will bring those that were strangers to him into an acquaintance with him, and it will be a blessed effect of their calamities. How much better is it, to be poor and know God, than to be rich, and ignorant of him?

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Seir - The seed of Esau, the Edomites. Seir was the mountain where they first planted themselves. Is like - Are no more a select people than others.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The side - That part of his country which was best fortified. Bethjeshimoth - An ancient city; it was a fortress toward the desert, which watched lest any should make an inroad on the country.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: With the Ammonites - As I have given Ammon, so I will with them give Moab to the Chaldeans, who will give it to the Arabians.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Teman - A country in the southern coast of Edom. Dedan - Adjoining to Edom.

entries.title: Ezekiel 25:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Cherethim - The bowmen, the strength of Philistia. The remnant - Who had escaped the sword of Samuel, David, Hezekiah, and of Psammetichus king of Egypt.
